result.builder:
Goal: make packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js take several files and stdin, for issue https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104. Deliver it as one pull request.

Context: the CLI currently takes one file (process.argv[2]), reads it with readFileSync, prints `${file}:${line}: ${error}` (newlines in the error replaced by spaces) for each problem from lint(text), and exits 0/1/2. Tests live in packages/jsonl-lint/test/cli.test.js (spawned CLI) and packages/jsonl-lint/test/lint.test.js. Zero dependencies, plain ES modules, node:test, Node 22+.

Steps:
1. Edit only packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js for behaviour. Do NOT touch packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js at all: lint(text) must stay byte-for-byte unchanged.
2. New CLI behaviour, `jsonl-lint <file> [<file> ...]`:
   - Check every named file in argument order. For each bad row print `<file>:<line>: <error>` on stdout, exactly the format used today for one file (file argument as given, newlines in the error replaced by a space). Output for each file is the same as running the tool on that file alone, concatenated in argument order.
   - An argument that is exactly `-` means read stdin (e.g. readFileSync(0, 'utf8')) and report its rows with the name `-` (e.g. `-:1: ...`).
   - If `-` appears more than once, it is a usage error: print a usage message on stderr and exit 2 (do this before checking any file).
   - No arguments: usage message on stderr, exit 2. Update the usage text to show `usage: jsonl-lint <file> [<file> ...]` and update the existing test in cli.test.js that matches the old usage text.
   - A file that can't be read: print `jsonl-lint: cannot read <file>: <message>` on stderr, keep going, and still check and report every other file.
   - Exit code: 2 if any file could not be read (or a usage error); otherwise 1 if any row in any file is bad; otherwise 0.
3. Add node:test tests in packages/jsonl-lint/test/cli.test.js (spawnSync the bin; pass stdin with the `input` option) covering at least, each as its own clearly named test:
   a. two clean files -> exit 0, empty stdout and stderr;
   b. one bad file among several clean ones -> exit 1, stdout has only that file's `<file>:<line>: ` lines, and order across several files follows argument order;
   c. stdin via `-`, clean input -> exit 0, no output;
   d. stdin via `-`, bad input -> exit 1, stdout lines start with `-:<line>: `;
   e. a missing file among good (and ideally one bad) files -> exit 2, stderr names the missing file, other files still checked and their bad rows still printed on stdout;
   f. two `-` arguments -> exit 2, message on stderr;
   g. no arguments -> exit 2, usage on stderr.
   Keep all existing tests passing.
4. Update packages/jsonl-lint/README.md: Usage section shows `node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> [<file> ...]`, explains that files are checked in order, that `-` reads stdin and is reported as `-`, that `-` may be given only once, and the exit codes (0 all clean, 1 any bad row in any file, 2 no file named / `-` twice / any file unreadable, with other files still checked).
5. Run `npm test` at the repository root and make it pass. Also sanity-check by hand, e.g. `printf '{bad}\n' | node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js packages/jsonl-lint/package.json -; echo $?` (expect `-:1: ...` and exit 1).
6. Commit, push, and open exactly one pull request on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test whose body contains the line `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104`. Wait for the `test` workflow (.github/workflows/test.yml) to finish on the PR head and fix anything until it is green.

text:
I've written both briefs (builder and verifier) for issue #104, and the harness accepted them.

**Builder brief:** it tells the builder to:
- change only `packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js` and leave `src/index.js` alone;
- add the seven CLI test cases the issue lists;
- update the old usage-text test, which no longer matches once the usage line changes;
- update the package README;
- open one PR that closes #104 and has a green `test` workflow.

**Verifier brief:** one check per acceptance line, in order. Each check runs the CLI on small fixture files in `/tmp/jlv`, the tests, `git diff` or `gh api`, and says what PASS and FAIL look like. A few extra suggestions sit under an Advisory heading.

**What I ran here, at the current commit:**
- The setup and the CLI commands run cleanly. They fail on the multi-file and `-` cases only because that feature isn't built yet.
- The `git diff` check on `src/index.js` passes.
- `npm test --workspace packages/jsonl-lint` passes all 12 existing tests.
- I first tried `node --test packages/jsonl-lint/test/` for the test check, but it fails at this commit, so I used `npm test --workspace packages/jsonl-lint` in the brief instead.
- **Not tested:** the `gh api` commands in check 6. This session has no GitHub access to the repo (HTTP 403), so I couldn't confirm they work. `gh pr view` also won't work, because GraphQL is blocked here, so the verifier brief uses REST calls instead.

Two decisions the issue doesn't settle, which I wrote into the builder brief:
- When `-` is given twice, the tool exits 2 before checking any file.
- An unreadable file takes priority: the exit is 2 even if another file has bad rows.
